Appendix D: Comparisons of Address Sample Survey Results by
Tenure, Length of Residency and Housing Type (Excluding "Don't
know" or "Not applicable")

For ease of comparison between subgroups, the questions show summarized responses for only the proportion of respondents giving a
positive answer; for example, the percent of respondents who "strongly or somewhat agreed" or gave a rating of "very or somewhat
positive" or "more favorable". Those who chose "Don't know" or "Not applicable" are not included in the percentages ­ it is the percent of
respondents "with an opinion."

The subgroup comparison tables contain the cross tabulations of survey questions by selected respondent characteristics. Chi-square or
ANOVA tests of significance were applied to these breakdowns of survey questions. A "p-value" of 0.05 or less indicates that there is less
than a 5% probability that differences observed between groups are due to chance; or in other words, a greater than 95% probability that
the differences observed in the selected categories of the sample represent "real" differences among those populations.

For each pair of subgroups that has a statistically significant difference, an uppercase letter denoting significance is shown in the category
with the larger column proportion. The letter denotes the category with the smaller column proportion from which it is statistically
different. Differences were marked as statistically significant if the probability that the differences were due to chance alone were less
than 5%. Where there are statistically significant differences by District, cells were also shaded grey. Items that have no uppercase letter
denotation in their column and that are also not referred to in any other column were not statistically different.

Appendix E: Comparisons of Address Sample Survey Results by
Types of Household Members (Excluding "Don't know" or "Not
applicable")

For ease of comparison between subgroups, the questions show summarized responses for only the proportion of respondents giving a
positive answer; for example, the percent of respondents who "strongly or somewhat agreed" or gave a rating of "very or somewhat
positive" or "more favorable". Those who chose "Don't know" or "Not applicable" are not included in the percentages ­ it is the percent of
respondents "with an opinion.

The subgroup comparison tables contain the cross tabulations of survey questions by selected respondent characteristics. Chi-square or
ANOVA tests of significance were applied to these breakdowns of survey questions. A "p-value" of 0.05 or less indicates that there is less
than a 5% probability that differences observed between groups are due to chance; or in other words, a greater than 95% probability that
the differences observed in the selected categories of the sample represent "real" differences among those populations.

For each pair of subgroups that has a statistically significant difference, an uppercase letter denoting significance is shown in the category
with the larger column proportion. The letter denotes the category with the smaller column proportion from which it is statistically
different. Differences were marked as statistically significant if the probability that the differences were due to chance alone were less
than 5%. Where there are statistically significant differences by District, cells were also shaded grey. Items that have no uppercase letter
denotation in their column and that are also not referred to in any other column were not statistically different.

Appendix F: Comparisons of Address Sample Survey Results by
Age, Gender and Race/Ethnicity (Excluding "Don't know" or "Not
applicable")

For ease of comparison between subgroups, the questions show summarized responses for only the proportion of respondents giving a
positive answer; for example, the percent of respondents who "strongly or somewhat agreed" or gave a rating of "very or somewhat
positive" or "more favorable". Those who chose "Don't know" or "Not applicable" are not included in the percentages ­ it is the percent of
respondents "with an opinion.

The subgroup comparison tables contain the cross tabulations of survey questions by selected respondent characteristics. Chi-square or
ANOVA tests of significance were applied to these breakdowns of survey questions. A "p-value" of 0.05 or less indicates that there is less
than a 5% probability that differences observed between groups are due to chance; or in other words, a greater than 95% probability that
the differences observed in the selected categories of the sample represent "real" differences among those populations.

For each pair of subgroups that has a statistically significant difference, an uppercase letter denoting significance is shown in the category
with the larger column proportion. The letter denotes the category with the smaller column proportion from which it is statistically
different. Differences were marked as statistically significant if the probability that the differences were due to chance alone were less
than 5%. Where there are statistically significant differences by District, cells were also shaded grey. Items that have no uppercase letter
denotation in their column and that are also not referred to in any other column were not statistically different.

Appendix G: Comparisons of Address Sample Survey Results by
Quadrant (Excluding "Don't know" or "Not applicable")

For ease of comparison between subgroups, the questions show summarized responses for only the proportion of respondents giving a
positive answer; for example, the percent of respondents who "strongly or somewhat agreed" or gave a rating of "very or somewhat
positive" or "more favorable". Those who chose "Don't know" or "Not applicable" are not included in the percentages ­ it is the percent of
respondents "with an opinion.

The subgroup comparison tables contain the cross tabulations of survey questions by selected respondent characteristics. Chi-square or
ANOVA tests of significance were applied to these breakdowns of survey questions. A "p-value" of 0.05 or less indicates that there is less
than a 5% probability that differences observed between groups are due to chance; or in other words, a greater than 95% probability that
the differences observed in the selected categories of the sample represent "real" differences among those populations.

For each pair of subgroups that has a statistically significant difference, an uppercase letter denoting significance is shown in the category
with the larger column proportion. The letter denotes the category with the smaller column proportion from which it is statistically
different. Differences were marked as statistically significant if the probability that the differences were due to chance alone were less
than 5%. Where there are statistically significant differences by District, cells were also shaded grey. Items that have no uppercase letter
denotation in their column and that are also not referred to in any other column were not statistically different.

Appendix H: Comparisons of Open Participation Survey Results by
Quadrant (Excluding "Don't know" or "Not applicable")

For ease of comparison between subgroups, the questions show summarized responses for only the proportion of respondents giving a
positive answer; for example, the percent of respondents who "strongly or somewhat agreed" or gave a rating of "very or somewhat
positive" or "more favorable". Those who chose "Don't know" or "Not applicable" are not included in the percentages ­ it is the percent of
respondents "with an opinion.

The subgroup comparison tables contain the cross tabulations of survey questions by selected respondent characteristics. Chi-square or
ANOVA tests of significance were applied to these breakdowns of survey questions. A "p-value" of 0.05 or less indicates that there is less
than a 5% probability that differences observed between groups are due to chance; or in other words, a greater than 95% probability that
the differences observed in the selected categories of the sample represent "real" differences among those populations.

For each pair of subgroups that has a statistically significant difference, an uppercase letter denoting significance is shown in the category
with the larger column proportion. The letter denotes the category with the smaller column proportion from which it is statistically
different. Differences were marked as statistically significant if the probability that the differences were due to chance alone were less
than 5%. Where there are statistically significant differences by District, cells were also shaded grey. Items that have no uppercase letter
denotation in their column and that are also not referred to in any other column were not statistically different.

Appendix I: Survey Methodology

Polco worked with the Design Workshop team and the City of Fayetteville to craft a survey to
capture community opinion about issues that will be addressed in the Parks System Master Plan.
The City of Fayetteville sponsored this research. For more information on this effort, please contact
Ted Jack at tjack@fayetteville-ar.gov.

This survey was implemented in August through September of 2021 through mailed invitations to
complete an online survey. Households were selected randomly from a USPS list of Fayetteville
households.

       · 6,000 households were randomly selected from a US Postal Service list of all residential
            addresses geocoded to be in the City of Fayetteville boundaries.

       · Each selected household received one postcard invitations and a follow up letter
            invitation. The invitation explained the purpose of the survey and provided a URL at
            which to complete the survey.

       · Additionally, City staff made outreach efforts to residents of multifamily units in areas
            where early indications showed low response.

Once this effort was underway, the City was provided a separate URL to use to share an invitation
to an "Open Participation" survey, where all residents who received notice through social media or
other communication channels could complete the survey.

Of the 6,000, a portion of which were returned undeliverable due to a vacancy. A total of 729
completed the random address sample survey for a response rate of 12% and an overall margin of
error of ±4%.

Additionally, 935 completed the Open Participation survey. The results of the Open Participation
are compared to those of the random address sample in an appendix of this report. The Address-
Based Sample was limited to addresses within city boundaries, but some respondents to the Open
Participation survey lived outside the City limits, their responses are shown in the geographic
comparisons, under separate cover. A few respondents to the surveys did not provide location
information.

The results from the random address sample (as well as, separately, the Open Participation effort)
were adjusted through a process known as weighting to be as reflective of Fayetteville's overall
population, as possible, using information available from the 2010 Census, 2017 American and
information from the USPS address sample. Statistical weights were applied to adjust the

Fayetteville Parks & Trails Proposed Maintenance Standards

FAYETTEVILLE PARKS PROPOSED
MAINTENANCE STANDARDS
Note: park standards can apply to a whole park or a
portion of a park; for example, a high use area of a
park may be maintained at a Level 2 standard, while
the lower use areas of the park may be maintained at a
Level 3 standard, as shown in the diagram to the right.

LEVEL 1

Maximum maintenance applied to high use, high recreational, economic, and cultural assets.
These are areas of high use and high visibility, with frequent programing occurring on site.
These areas require daily maintenance for restroom and trash pickup and have high quality
horticulture elements that require maintenance multiple times per week.

Parks in this category include: Square Gardens and Ramble Civic Space

INSPECTIONS
Quality inspections done weekly.

TURF CARE
Turf is mowed at 1-2 times per week and is irrigated with multiple turf maintenance practices
occurring based on seasons. Turf maintenance practices to keep a weed- and pest-free turf are
utilized on an as needed basis.

LITTER CONTROL
Includes pick up of litter on grounds. Litter pickup and trash cans emptied minimum of once per
day, seven days per week.

RESTROOMS
Open 24 hours per day, seven days per week. Cleaned 1-2 times per day.

PLAYGROUNDS
Inspected for safety regularly based on usage. Inspections include visual, mechanical, and a
minimum once annual inspection by a certified playground inspector. Loose surfaces groomed
weekly, and solid surfaces cleaned weekly.

FACILITIES
Kept tidy and clear of debris, and are cleaned prior to and after reservations and events.

Fayetteville Parks & Trails Proposed Maintenance Standards                                       p. 1
SURFACES
At no time does an accumulation of dirt or leaves distract from looks or safety of area.

FURNISHINGS
Kept clean and functional. Minimal tolerance of visible wear and tear.

IRRIGATION
Frequency of use follows rainfall, temperature, maintenance schedules, programming, etc.
Inspected once per month. Level 1 irrigated areas are high priority areas in times of drought.

LANDSCAPE PLANTINGS
Maximum care (water, fertilizing, weeding, etc.) is done at minimum of twice per week in growing
season.

REPAIRS
Immediate response to all elements of design when problems are discovered.

LEVEL 2

High levels of maintenance applied to a high-quality diverse landscape associated with high
use and high visibility. Maintenance is typically performed multiple times per week.

Park spaces in this category include: High Use areas of Community and Regional Parks and
Athletic Complexes

INSPECTIONS
Quality inspections done monthly.

TURF CARE
Turf is mowed at 1-2 times per week and is irrigated with multiple turf maintenance practices
occurring based on seasons. Turf maintenance practices to keep a weed and pest free turf are
utilized on an as needed basis.

LITTER CONTROL
Includes pick up of litter on grounds. Litter pickup and trash cans emptied minimum of once per
day, five to seven days per week.

RESTROOMS
Open minimum of 12 hours per day, seven days per week or when facility is open. Cleaned once
per day unless events require increased service.

PLAYGROUNDS
Inspected for safety monthly based on usage. Inspections include visual, mechanical, and a
minimum once annual inspection by a certified playground inspector. Loose surfaces groomed
every other week, and solid surfaces cleaned weekly.

FACILITIES
Kept tidy and clear of debris, and are cleaned prior to and after reservations.

Fayetteville Parks & Trails Proposed Maintenance Standards  p. 2
SURFACES
Kept reasonably clear of dirt and leaves that distract from looks or safety of area. In the fall leaves
are removed once per week.

FURNISHINGS
Kept clean and functional. Minimal tolerance of visible wear and tear.

IRRIGATION
Frequency of use follows rainfall, temperature, maintenance schedules, programming, etc.
Inspected once per month. Level 2 irrigated areas are priority areas in times of drought following
Level 1 areas.

LANDSCAPE PLANTINGS
Maximum care (water, fertilizing, weeding, etc.) is done at minimum of once per week in growing
season.

REPAIRS
Immediate response to priority elements of design when problems are discovered.

LEVEL 3

Consistent, quality maintenance for regularly attended, lower use parks and lower use areas
of high use parks. Maintenance should ensure a safe, attractive, and functional site and
accommodate this steady and medium levels of visitors. Maintenance is typically performed
once to twice per week.

Park areas in this category include: lower but still actively used areas of Regional and Community
Parks, and high use areas of the most popular neighborhood parks such as Gordon Long west of
creek

INSPECTIONS
Quality inspections done every other month.

TURF CARE
Mowed at least once every seven working days in growing season. Keeping a weed-free turf is not
prioritized.

LITTER CONTROL
Trash cans emptied minimum three days per week.

RESTROOMS
Open minimum 12 hours per day, seven days per week. Cleaned minimum of once every other
day.

PLAYGROUNDS
Inspected for safety routinely based on usage. Inspections include visual, mechanical, and a
minimum once annual inspection by a certified playground inspector. Loose surfaces groomed
monthly, and solid surfaces cleaned twice per month.

Fayetteville Parks & Trails Proposed Maintenance Standards  p. 3
FACILITIES
Kept tidy and clear of debris, and are cleaned prior to and after reservations.

SURFACES
Cleaned regularly. Repaired, repainted or replaced when appearances have noticeably
deteriorated.

FURNISHINGS
Kept clean and functional. Tolerance of wear and tear that does not impede use and safety.

IRRIGATION
Frequency of use follows rainfall, temperature, maintenance schedules, etc. Inspected once per
month. Medium priority areas in times of drought.

LANDSCAPE PLANTINGS
Floral plantings are limited in size and complexity. Care (water, fertilizing, weeding, etc.) is done
once every three weeks in growing season.

REPAIRS
Done whenever safety, function, or appearance is in question.

LEVEL 4

Consistent but moderate maintenance for typical neighborhood parks (relatively lower but
regular use). Maintenance is typically performed every week to every other week.

Park areas in this category include: Finger and Rodney Ryan Parks (mowed areas)

INSPECTIONS
Quality inspections done every other month.

TURF CARE
Mowed at least once every seven working days in growing season. Turf is not managed, except
through mowing, for weeds.

LITTER CONTROL
Trash cans emptied minimum of once per week.

RESTROOMS
Not always provided. If so, cleaned 1-2 times per week at minimum.

PLAYGROUNDS
Inspected for safety routinely based on usage. Inspections include visual, mechanical, and a
minimum once annual inspection by a certified playground inspector. Loose surfaces groomed
weekly, solid surfaces cleaned every other week.

FACILITIES
Kept clear of debris, and are cleaned prior to and after reservations, but not more than once per
day if multiple reservations.

Fayetteville Parks & Trails Proposed Maintenance Standards                                             p. 4
SURFACES
Cleaned regularly. Repaired, repainted or replaced when appearances have noticeably
deteriorated.

FURNISHINGS
Kept clean and functional. Tolerance of moderate wear and tear that does not impede use and
safety.

IRRIGATION
Frequency of use follows rainfall, temperature, maintenance schedules, etc. Inspected once per
month. Low priority areas in times of drought.

LANDSCAPE PLANTINGS
Minimal care unless outside maintenance is supplied.

"NATURAL" AREAS
Care every other month during growing season (pruning, invasive species control, etc.), prioritizing
high-quality natural areas. Litter removal weekly. Immediate removal of safety hazards.

REPAIRS
Done whenever safety, function, or appearance is in question.

LEVEL 5

Moderate to low level of maintenance associated with lower use parks and those with limited
amenities. Maintenance is typically performed weekly to monthly.

Park areas in this category include: low use neighborhood parks with no playgrounds and natural
areas with few amenities

INSPECTIONS
Quality inspections done twice annually as staff time allows.

TURF CARE
Mowed at least once every ten working days in growing season. Turf is not managed, except
through mowing, for weeds.

LITTER CONTROL
Trash cans emptied a minimum of once per week.

RESTROOMS
n/a; not provided

PLAYGROUNDS
n/a; not provided

SURFACES
Cleaned on complaint basis. Repaired or replaced as budget allows.

Fayetteville Parks & Trails Proposed Maintenance Standards  p. 5
FURNISHINGS
Kept clean and functional. Tolerance of moderate wear and tear that maximizes life cycle of
furnishings.

NATURAL AREAS
Seasonal care (pruning, invasive species control, etc.), prioritizing high-quality natural areas.
Immediate removal of safety hazards.

REPAIRS
Done whenever safety or function is in question.

LEVEL 6

Lower level of maintenance associated with limited use areas. Maintenance is typically
performed monthly or seasonally.

Park areas in this category include: low use park and natural areas with minimal amenities

INSPECTIONS
Quality inspections done annually as staff time allows.

TURF CARE
Conservation lawn approach for interior turf. Turf edges mowed every ten working days in growing
season. Turf is not managed, except through mowing, for weeds.

LITTER CONTROL
Minimum of twice per month.

RESTROOMS
Typically not provided. If provided, open 6-8 hours per day, seven days per week and cleaned at
least twice per week.

SURFACES
Cleaned on complaint basis. Repaired or replaced as budget allows.

FURNISHINGS
Kept functional. Tolerance of moderate wear and tear. Patrons may need to clean benches and
tables to use.

NATURAL AREAS
Seasonal care (pruning, invasive species control, etc.), prioritizing high-quality natural areas.
Immediate removal of safety hazards.

REPAIRS
Done whenever safety or function is in question.

Fayetteville Parks & Trails Proposed Maintenance Standards  p. 6
LEVEL 7

Lowest levels of maintenance associated with remote natural areas and undeveloped parcels.
Maintenance is typically performed as needed or on a complaint basis.

Park areas in this category include: Undeveloped parkland, regional lake surfaces

INSPECTIONS
Not performed.

TURF CARE
Conservation lawn approach. Turf is not managed, except through mowing, for weeds.

LITTER CONTROL
Typically performed via volunteer efforts.

SURFACES
Cleaned on complaint basis. Repaired or replaced as budget allows.

FURNISHINGS
Kept functional. Tolerance of high wear and tear that maximizes life cycle costs but does not
impede safety. Patrons may need to clean benches and tables to use.

VEGETATION
No staff time spent on pruning, invasive species control, etc. unless a management plan is in place
targeting specific efforts. Only safety related work is approached immediately (e.g., dead trees not
posing a safety threat onto trails are allowed to fall and decay in the landscape).

LAKE SURFACES
Occasional maintenance to control excessive aquatic plants or fish as budget allows.

REPAIRS
Done whenever safety or function is in question.

Fayetteville Parks & Trails Proposed Maintenance Standards  p. 7
FAYETTEVILLE TRAILS PROPOSED MAINTENANCE STANDARDS

HARD SURFACE TRAILS (8' WIDE AND
ABOVE)

Maintenance of hard surface trails and the immediate
space at their edges is set at a minimum of Level
Four (see Parks Maintenance Standards), but
maintenance may be higher reflecting the standards
of the space the trail is passing through. See
accompanying graphic.

SOFT SURFACE NAMED TRAILS

Soft Surface Trails are all named trails and have four
classifications of care. These levels of care will help
determine a maintenance need per linear foot.
Unnamed trails will be maintained at the same level
of the area they are located in (e.g., unnamed trail in a
Level 3 park area will be maintained at Level 3).

SST1
Centennial, Cross country, MTB, and cyclocross race
trails
During the growing season, trails receive biweekly
mowing/string trimming and pruning of woody
vegetation. Trails are inspected bi-weekly or after heavy rains. Perform tread repairs and remove
any identified hazards as noted in inspections. Trails may be groomed before major events.

SST2
High use biking and hiking trails with technical features (e.g., downhill trails and skill courses)
During the growing season, trails receive monthly mowing/string trimming and pruning of woody
vegetation. Trails are inspected monthly or after heavy rains. Perform tread repairs and remove
any identified hazards as noted in inspections.

SST3
High use simple biking and hiking trails with few to no technical features (e.g., Lake Fayetteville
and the Fayetteville Traverse)
During the growing season, trails receive monthly mowing/string trimming and pruning of woody
vegetation. Trails are inspected monthly and tread repairs are made and identified hazards
removed as needed based on inspection results.

SST4
Low use simple trails (Examples: Lake Wilson & Lake Sequoyah trails)
Minimal maintenance is performed. Hazards and storm damage are attended to as they are
reported.

skills are needed to manage and run the
